original_test_intent: Exercise repeated BMC file upload and removal at 0C and +5% 5V/3.3V rails while verifying data integrity, BMC availability, storage health and absence of unexpected events.
original_method: Do not execute until the exact BMC storage target, protocol/account, test-file identity/size/hash, upload/remove semantics, repetition or duration, capacity/wear limits, integrity oracle and recovery are approved; after resolution, control dew point/high rails, perform bounded transfers with per-iteration hashes/free-space/service evidence, then clean up, warm safely and restore nominal state.
manual_activity: After resolution, operator controls cold/high-rail conditions and supervises bounded BMC transfer/cleanup.
required_inputs: BMC firmware/storage partition and approved scratch path
Exact repetitions or duration/rate and remove semantics
Reserve/free-space, wear, service-latency and SEL limits
0C dew-point/+5% rail limits, abort, cleanup and recovery
safety_requirements: Never guess BMC paths or fill persistent storage
Use non-sensitive deterministic content and least privilege
Abort on low reserve, integrity mismatch, service loss, wear/error or environmental fault
agent_execution_scope: May validate an approved plan and analyze transfer/hash/service artifacts
Must not choose BMC target, upload arbitrary data, remove files or decide verdict
engineer_actions: Approve cold profile and supervise execution

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Physical boundary is correct, but no command can be safely derived without protocol, path, file and loop semantics.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: BLOCKED; after approval, use the pinned authenticated transfer method only against the approved scratch path with preflight reserve and per-iteration verification.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BMC upload/remove repetition at 0C and +5% 5V/3.3V is retained; the source gives no valid duration/count to invent.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use bounded deterministic transfers with hash, free-space, service-health and cleanup evidence synchronized to environmental data.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds target/protocol/file identity, resource limits, measurable integrity, condensation controls and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Uploading an arbitrary file once or writing to an unspecified partition cannot represent repeated BMC storage stress.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: An undefined loop may exhaust flash, wear storage or remove system files; 'upload normally' has no measurable integrity or latency threshold.

project_override_considerations: BMC owner defines approved scratch storage, protocol, repetition/duration, wear budget, reserve and service-availability tolerance.
expected_evidence: Test-file size/hash and exact loop specification
Free-space/storage error/wear and BMC service telemetry
Cleanup, safe warm-up and nominal post-health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently asks for repeated BMC upload/remove, but omits essential operation and limit semantics rather than stating contradictory ones.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Target path, transfer mechanism, file, bounds and recovery are indeterminate; guessing any of them creates persistent-storage and availability risk.

engineering_decision_pending.question: Resolve Stability row43 Wistron-Margin-00042-V003: approve BMC firmware/storage scratch path and reserve, console/SSH/SCP/API protocol/account/permissions, test file size/hash/content, repetition count or duration/rate, integrity/free-space/wear/SEL criteria, 0C humidity/dew-point/+5% rail limits, abort, cleanup, safe warm-up and recovery.

review_improvement: Stops an unbounded, target-undefined BMC storage operation and defines the missing integrity, capacity and recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Repeated upload/remove stresses both the transfer service and persistent BMC storage. Without a scratch-path boundary and free-space/wear limits, the test could fill or damage a firmware partition. Per-iteration hashes and service availability are necessary because a successful transport response does not prove stored content integrity.
